summary: Recorded the snapshot-enabled receipt, resolved the registered gap and opened the next lead. Receipt fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 (all five tests passed) showed the same signature as the NoSnapshot run with an Entry whose Snapshot::use_snapshots() is true: the two re-synchronized followers ended at accepted index 7 over six indices of content with read(5) returning None and a one-element decided-log read (events 51, 52) and the leader ended at accepted 6 with decided 7, its reconfiguration endpoint false and its decided log unreadable (event 53), against a baseline in which all three reported 6/6 with a six-element decided read (events 48-50); comparisons requiring the StopSign at index 5, the six-element decided read and the consistent endpoints were violated at 51-53 while the baselines held. So the defect is not tied to the entry configuration. Updates: the interpretation now covers all five receipts separately with same-run controls and joint_history, with the snapshot result integrated and the limitation about the untested snapshot option replaced by a note that compaction calls themselves remain unexercised; the three indexed behaviours/facts are re-conditioned on both entry configurations and the fifth receipt's indices; the gap asking about the snapshot option and about a leader's own accepted index is answered as resolved on both halves (leader-side inflation witnessed in receipt dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea event 13, snapshot option reproduced in events 51-53). A child question was registered for a different pairing in the same mechanism area: handle_majority_promises adopts the maximum decided index over all promises but the log from the single maximum promise, so the adopted decided index may exceed the entries the leader holds when those two come from different nodes; no execution was requested this turn. Incomplete: that new question's source trace and probe, loss- and timer-triggered re-synchronization, larger clusters, persistence across restarts, and compaction (trim/snapshot calls) themselves.
